dependency_notes: Linear dependency chain S1..S8 plus a final FR-A7 integration story S9. S1 (Dispatcher seam + choke-point drop) is the foundation — every later story consumes the AuthenticatedSender sibling arg it introduces. S2 (attribution refactor) does the one-time mechanical signature propagation into every handler plus signature-only threading into the two second-hop modules (Reactions, Edits) and the static-scan; S3-S8 build authorization/actor-rule logic on top of that already-threaded sender. S6 deliberately spans the Chat store + Structured parse modules per architecture.md's explicit 'hidden coupling... biggest work item' call-out (system messages are kind-9 rows; ingest-time enforcement touches chat persistence, unread counts, and notification invariants, not just the parser) rather than forcing an artificial split. S4 also verifies (test-only, no code change) that chatPersistence.ts's Tombstone re-check inherits the authenticated sender from the Edits module, per architecture.md's explicit inheritance note. AC-GATE-11 (full 60-test e2e gate) is an epic-level exit gate, not a per-story AC, and is intentionally not assigned to any story. AC-MV-1, AC-MV-2, AC-MV-3 are Manual Validation items (owner: product owner) — not stories; they record that this epic is readiness-only (the seam is fed the claimed pubkey until the out-of-scope MLS backbone lands) and that the project's impersonation finding stays open. S9 is the FR-A7 integration story: it owns all five Cross-Cutting Invariants ACs (AC-XCUT-1..5), each of which carries a 'Spans modules:' line in acceptance-criteria.md, and runs strictly last, verified against the real, already-landed producers from S1/S3/S4/S5/S7 (never mocked).
mock_resolution_plan: No temporary mocks are introduced by this epic. All cross-story data is the live AuthenticatedSender value threaded from S1, or the existing GroupAdminsProvider + live-roster accessor already registered in production wiring (MarmotContext.tsx) and reused as injected deps.

invariants: authenticity is always 'claimed' under this epic's app-side resolver stub; only the out-of-scope MLS backbone can ever produce 'mls'
pubkey equals rumor.pubkey unless the dev-only override hook (gated NODE_ENV !== 'production') injected a divergent value
resolved once per rumor, after deserialize and strictly before markSeen, so a dropped (sender-mismatched) rumor never poisons the per-group dedup LRU (AC-XCUT-1)
is a sibling argument to the rumor on every handler call, never a field mutated on the shared per-group DispatcherContext

stories.name: authenticated-sender-seam
stories.title: Per-message authenticated-sender seam + choke-point drop
stories.description: Foundation story. Adds AuthenticatedSender { pubkey, authenticity } as a per-message sibling argument (not a field on the shared per-group DispatcherContext) in applicationRumorDispatcher.ts. The app-side resolver closure (wired in MarmotContext.tsx where dispatcherCtx + buildDispatcher(...).subscribe(...) are set up, ~L1501-1612) defaults to { pubkey: rumor.pubkey, authenticity: 'claimed' } and is overridable via a dev-only hook (window.__fewTest precedent, gated NODE_ENV !== 'production') so tests can inject a divergent sender. The dispatcher resolves the sender after deserialize but strictly before markSeen and before fan-out: if rumor.pubkey !== sender.pubkey, the rumor is dropped (no handler runs, no markSeen, so the dedup LRU is never poisoned) and an 'unauthenticatedMessage' diagnostic is dev-logged. This story changes only the dispatcher entry point and wiring; propagating the new sender argument into every handler body is S2.

excludes: second-hop authorization logic in reactions/api.ts and messageEdits/api.ts (S2 threads signatures, S4 adds edit/delete authorization logic)

stories.name: attribution-refactor-and-second-hop
stories.title: Attribution refactor across all handlers + second-hop signature threading + static ban
stories.description: Propagates handle(rumor, ctx, sender) into every rumor handler wrapper and inner function (chat, reaction, poll open/vote/close, leave, call_notice, group_renamed, member_admitted, invite_lifecycle, profile, profile-request) and their construction sites in registerHandlers.ts. Repoints every attribution/authorization read from rumor.pubkey to sender.pubkey — including chatHandler.ts:86's high-blast-radius ChatMessage.senderPubkey assignment — while preserving the chatHandler.ts:108 own-send echo guard as a scoped, explicitly-commented non-attribution read. Threads sender as a new argument into the two second-hop modules' entry points, reactions/api.ts's applyInboundRumor and messageEdits/api.ts's applyDeleteEditSignal, doing the signature change and a basic field-swap (rumor.pubkey -> sender.pubkey) only — the deeper stored-sender comparison logic specific to AC-EDIT-7 lands in S4. Adds a vitest source-scan (precedent: zodBoundary.test.ts) that fails the build on any rumor.pubkey read inside handlers/ outside an explicit, documented allow-list, scoped to handlers/ only (directMessages.ts, pairingAck.ts, and gift-wrap code are already seal-authenticated and out of scope), plus targeted assertions that both second-hop modules authorize on the passed sender. Preserves the existing trust-model comment block (deleteEditHandler.ts:29-56) verbatim. Updates every app/tests/unit/marmot/*.test.ts call site touched by the signature change.

excludes: poll actor rules and tally recompute (S5)
announcement actor rules and ingest gate (S6)

stories.name: forced-removal-sender-gate
stories.title: Forced-removal rule: leave_intent subject === sender
stories.description: leaveHandler.ts's enqueueLeave(ctx.groupId, payload.pubkey) is only called when payload.pubkey (the subject) === sender.pubkey; a leave_intent naming a different subject than its authenticated sender is not enqueued and not rendered as a departure. Readiness-only per AC-MV-1: under the app-layer-only stub the attacker controls both fields via the dev override hook, so this does not yet stop a real forced removal — that requires the out-of-scope MLS backbone.

stories.name: edit-delete-authorization
stories.title: Edit/delete authorization on authenticated sender (+ tombstone inheritance verification)
stories.description: applyDeleteEditSignal (messageEdits/api.ts) rejects an edit/delete whose signal's authenticated sender differs from the target message's stored authenticated sender (ChatMessage.senderPubkey, now populated from sender.pubkey by S2) — no tombstone written, no edit applied — unless the separate admin-delete path is satisfied via GroupAdminsProvider. Also verifies (test-only, no independent code change) that chatPersistence.ts's TombstoneAuthorization re-check inherits this same authenticated value from the edits module, per architecture.md's explicit inheritance note for the third hop.

excludes: the second-hop signature threading itself, already done in S2

stories.name: poll-actor-rules-and-tally-recompute
stories.title: Poll actor rules: creator binding, vote/close authorization, tally recompute
stories.description: On poll_open, the stored creatorPubkey is bound to sender.pubkey; any creatorPubkey value present in the payload is ignored. poll_vote is recorded keyed to sender.pubkey under the poll:voter key. poll_close is authorized only when sender.pubkey equals the poll's stored creatorPubkey (not an admin). On an accepted poll_close, the displayed tally is recomputed from stored PollVote rows (a green-field addition — no existing recompute path today) and never taken from the close message's results/totalVoters fields, so a close carrying forged counts still shows the true tally.

stories.name: announcement-actor-rules-and-ingest-gate
stories.title: Enum announcement per-type actor rules + ingest-time enforcement gate
stories.description: Deliberately spans the Chat store and Structured parse modules, per architecture.md's explicit 'hidden coupling... biggest work item' call-out: system messages are literal kind-9 rows, so ingest-time enforcement necessarily touches chat persistence, unread counts, and notification-domain invariants, not just the parser — the epic's own spec scopes this as one story rather than an artificial split. Enforces per-type actor rules in chatHandler.ts, before deps.appendMessage is called: admin-actor gate (via GroupAdminsProvider) for group_renamed, invite_lifecycle('accepted'), and member_admitted, with an ingest-time, non-retroactive roster check for the two admission-subject types (member_admitted, invite_lifecycle('accepted')) — checked once at first ingest and persisted as a flag, never re-evaluated on a later groupDataVersion bump. invite_lifecycle('invited'/'declined') and invite_cancelled render the subject as an unverified claim and are never roster-gated, by design. call_notice's displayed actor is sender.pubkey (parseStructured.ts stops rendering the payload's initiator field). A rejected announcement (non-admin actor, or a failed ingest-time roster check) produces no chat row, no setChatVersion bump, no unread increment, and no notification. Reuses the existing GroupAdminsProvider + live-roster accessor (getGroupMembers) via injected deps, reactive on groupDataVersion — no new provider is built. ALSO (Fable S3 Stage-2 finding 2, folded into S6): the kind-9 leave_intent DEPARTURE ANNOUNCEMENT (the "X left the group" chat row rendered from the self-reported structured.pubkey/name at ChatBox.tsx) is a SELF-CLAIM — apply a subject===sender rule at ingest so a forged "X left" for X != authenticated sender does not render (mirrors the S3 enqueue-side rule and the group_renamed attribute-to-sender pattern). Add scope: app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/chatHandler.ts leave_intent branch + parseStructured.ts leave_intent variant. ALSO (Fable S5 Stage-2 finding F1, routed to S6): the kind-9 poll_close CHAT ANNOUNCEMENT (PollStoreContext.tsx close bubble) currently carries the closer's self-reported results/totalVoters and ChatBox renders them VERBATIM via PollChatResults, appended by chatHandler with NO actor gate — so the AC-POLL-4 tally forgery the product owner approved closing is still alive on the chat-bubble surface, and any member (not just the creator) can post a fake poll-closed bubble. S6 MUST: (a) creator-gate the poll_close announcement at ingest (only the poll's authenticated creator), and (b) render the RECOMPUTED tally (resolve the stored Poll by pollId and recompute from stored votes) rather than the payload counts. Also the poll_open bubble displays structured.creatorPubkey (spoofable X-created-a-poll author) — attribute to sender. Add scope: ChatBox.tsx poll_open/poll_close render + chatHandler poll-announcement ingest.

stories.name: shared-envelope-verifier-and-profiles
stories.title: Shared inner-envelope verifier + forwarded-profile attribution
stories.description: Generalizes parseProfilePayload (profileSync.ts) into one shared inner-envelope verifier that runs once, before fan-out, for forwardable kinds (today: profile only). The verifier applies the hardening set applicable now: valid inner signature, correct inner event kind, group-binding for group-scoped kinds via a per-kind binding policy (profile is group-binding-exempt), and one-shot consumption keyed on the inner event id. Profiles are explicitly exempt from the actor-in-roster check (context-free, identity-scoped — roster-gating would degrade a departed member's late profile to a raw key). profileHandler.ts becomes one caller of the shared verifier and repoints the unsigned/legacy payloadToMemberProfile(rumor.pubkey, ...) fallback to the authenticated sender.

stories.name: profile-request-drop-and-send-fail-closed
stories.title: Profile-request bind (via seam) + meta-event send fails closed
stories.description: The profile-request drop itself requires no new handler logic: kind-30 rumors are already one of the kinds exercised by S1's choke-point drop (AC-SEAM-1), and profileRequestHandler.ts's auto-reply is target-driven with no rumor.pubkey reads. This story adds send-side fail-closed behavior: if a forwardable inner signature cannot be produced (locked or absent NIP-07 signer), the meta-event is not emitted and not actioned locally. Surfacing is per path — an interactive (user-initiated) send shows a visible, i18n-backed error; a background/relay send dev-logs the failure and relies on the existing profile-request retry machinery, showing no UI error.

stories.name: cross-cutting-order-and-redelivery-invariants
stories.title: Cross-cutting order-sensitivity invariants (dedup, tally, debounce, edit-order, profile LWW)
stories.description: FR-A7 integration story. Owns all five Cross-Cutting Invariants ACs from acceptance-criteria.md, each of which carries a 'Spans modules:' line written by the planner's Mode-1 derivation from architecture.md's Order-Sensitive Composition signal. Runs strictly last, verified against the real, already-landed producers from S1 (Dispatcher), S3 (Leave), S4 (Edits 2nd hop + Tombstone 3rd hop), S5 (Poll), and S7 (Shared verifier + Profiles) — never mocked, per the Mock Strategy FR-A7 exception. Five whole-flow property tests, each quantified over a generator of orderings/interleavings rather than a single hand-picked sequence: (1) a rumor dropped for sender mismatch leaves no trace in the dedup LRU, and a subsequent legitimate redelivery of the same id still fans out exactly once, regardless of arrival order; (2) the displayed poll tally equals the recomputation from exactly the PollVote rows currently stored, for any arrival order/subset/duplication of votes, and never varies with the close message's claimed counts; (3) a removal is enqueued for a subject if and only if that subject's own leave-intent had payload.pubkey === sender.pubkey, across any interleaving of concurrent/duplicate leave-intents within the debounce window; (4) edit/delete authorization outcomes are identical regardless of signal/target arrival order or resolvePendingSignalsForSlot's resolution order, and this holds identically at both the edits module and the tombstone re-check it feeds; (5) merged MemberProfile state after two profile envelopes (including a self-authored/forwarded pair of the same signed inner event) is identical regardless of delivery order and equals the profile with the greatest updatedAt, and the verifier's one-shot consumption applies a duplicate inner event id at most once regardless of which copy arrives first. Exempt from Module Ownership principle 5's one-module-per-story rule by design (FR-A7/D6): this exemption licenses reaching across S1/S3/S4/S5/S7's modules to verify the assembled whole, and does not license re-implementing any of their logic.
